take_homes: Split agents only on access, dialect or stance. Most of my agents fail all three tests.
Handoffs are where it breaks. A curator can silently drop a conflicting number, and a synthesizer with no framework just averages.
Nothing in the pipeline checks whether the final briefing is true, and I don't have a check for that.

monday.move: Audit the existing engineering agents against the three split tests. Then add a conflict check, listing disagreeing numbers and sources, to the curator step of the sales-setup I was going to build.
monday.who: me, plus one engineer who owns the agent setup
monday.stop_condition: If the audit finds no seam that loses information, stop and leave the setup as it is.
monday.blocker: Nobody outside engineering has asked for the sales setup, and I haven't decided who maintains it.

misconception.why: The curator keeping one of two numbers, and a synthesis that sounds confident and can't be verified, showed me a good agent can still give bad output. I skipped the review step earlier and had no idea what I'd missed. I'm not fully convinced that checking applies to me, though.

one_line: Good on when not to split agents and where the handoffs break, but the pace is slow for anyone who already runs agents and it leaves the 'is it true' question open.
